# Sirach Chapter 39 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 39 | **Agents Consulted:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA

---

## Council Notes

Chapter 39 completes the scribe-versus-laborer comparison from 38:24 by fully developing the scribal ideal (vv. 1–11), then launches into a doxology praising God's works (vv. 12–35). Verses 1–11 are one of antiquity's clearest formulations of the life of religious scholarship: study, travel, service to rulers, prayer, inspiration, teaching, and lasting fame. The doxological section contains Ben Sira's great affirmation: "All the works of the Lord are very good" (v. 16), echoing Genesis 1:31. The apparently contradictory claim — that destructive things (wind, fire, beasts) are also good (v. 27) — is resolved by the "in their time" principle: everything has its proper function and season. The refrain "no one can say, 'What is this?'" (vv. 17, 21) is a rhetorical device against questioning divine providence.

---

39:1 But the one who devotes himself to the study of the law of the Most High will seek the wisdom of all the ancients and occupy himself with prophecies.

39:2 He will preserve the discourses of famous men and penetrate the subtleties of figures of speech.

39:3 He will seek out the hidden meanings of proverbs and be occupied with the riddles of parables.

39:4 He will serve among great men and appear before rulers; he will travel through the lands of foreign peoples, for he tests the good and the evil in human experience.

39:5 He will set his heart to rise early to seek the Lord who made him, and will pray before the Most High; he will open his mouth in prayer and make supplication for his sins.

39:6 If the great Lord wills it, he will be filled with the spirit of understanding; he will pour forth his own words of wisdom and give thanks to the Lord in prayer.

39:7 He will direct his counsel and knowledge aright, and meditate on his secrets.

39:8 He will reveal instruction in his teaching, and will glory in the law of the Lord's covenant.

39:9 Many will praise his understanding, and it will never be blotted out; his memory will not disappear, and his name will live through all generations.

39:10 Nations will recount his wisdom, and the congregation will declare his praise.

39:11 If he lives long, he will leave a name greater than a thousand, and if he goes to his rest, it is enough for him.

39:12 I still have more to say, which I have thought upon, and I am as full as the moon at the full.

39:13 Listen to me, O holy children, and bud like a rose growing beside a flowing stream;

39:14 send forth fragrance like incense, and put forth blossoms like a lily. Scatter your fragrance and sing a hymn of praise; bless the Lord for all his works.

39:15 Ascribe greatness to his name and give thanks to him with praise, with songs on your lips and with stringed instruments; and this is what you shall say in thanksgiving:

39:16 "All the works of the Lord are very good, and whatever he commands will be done in its time."

39:17 No one can say, "What is this?" or "Why is that?" — for at the right time all things will be sought out. At his command the waters stood in a heap, and the reservoirs of water at the word of his mouth.

39:18 At his word whatever pleases him is accomplished, and no one can restrict his saving power.

39:19 The deeds of all flesh are before him, and nothing can be hidden from his eyes.

39:20 From age to age he beholds them, and nothing is wonderful in his sight.

39:21 No one can say, "What is this?" or "Why is that?" — for everything has been created for a purpose.

39:22 His blessing covers the dry land like a river and saturates it like a flood.

39:23 As he turned a well-watered land into salt flats, so his wrath strips the nations of their heritage.

39:24 His ways are smooth for the holy, but full of obstacles for the wicked.

39:25 Good things were created from the beginning for the good, and likewise evil things for sinners.

39:26 The basic necessities of human life are water and fire and iron and salt, wheat flour and milk and honey, the juice of the grape and oil and clothing.

39:27 All these are good for the devout, but they turn into evils for sinners.

39:28 There are winds that were created for punishment; in their fury they can move mountains; in the time of destruction they pour out their strength and appease the anger of their Maker.

39:29 Fire and hail and famine and pestilence — all these have been created for punishment;

39:30 the teeth of wild beasts and scorpions and vipers, and the avenging sword for the destruction of the wicked;

39:31 all these will rejoice in his commands and stand ready on earth for his service; in their seasons they will not be lacking.

39:32 Therefore from the beginning I have been convinced of this, and having thought it through I have left it in writing:

39:33 all the works of the Lord are good, and he will supply every need in its proper time.

39:34 No one can say, "This is worse than that," for all things will prove good in their due season.

39:35 So now sing praises with all your heart and voice, and bless the name of the Lord.
